mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the FEDFUNDS rate increased by more than 0.25% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within 3 months signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where the UNRATE dropped by more than 0.5% within 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) over 3 consecutive months signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where RSAFS increased for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within a month signals increased economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO increased by more than 1% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% within the same month, it signals a robust labor market, boosting consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200k and UNRATE drop > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% within a month signals a strong demand for housing, which boosts related industries and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where HOUST increased by more than 5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) remains unchanged within the same month, it signals inflationary pressure without a corresponding monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% and FEDFUNDS unchanged in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decrease in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 1% within a quarter signals a contraction in economic activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where GDPC1 decreased by more than 1% within a quarter.
